In the beginning, the aircraft had an all-economy 3-3 configuration, with the first four front rows sold as Smile Plus Class. During the rehabilitation process of Thai Airways, it was announced that Thai Smile would be merged into the mainline. The aircraft were consecutively transferred to Thai Airways from May 2023 until January 2024, and the retrofit plan was announced later in February 2024. The plan includes installing 12 new business class seats, replacing the former economy seats, arranged in a 2-2 configuration across the first three rows, along with wireless in-flight entertainment. The retrofitted aircraft will primarily operate on domestic routes once the Airbus A321neo has been delivered.{{Cite news |last=Wancharoen |first=Supoj |date=25 February 2023 |title=Thai Smile-THAI merger 'to cut losses' |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/general/2514539/thai-smile-thai-merger-to-cut-losses |access-date=17 October 2025 |work=Bangkok Post |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Thai Airways News & Announcements {{!}} Thai Airways International |url=https://www.thaiairways.com/en_JP/news/news_announcement/news_detail/new-bc-a320-event.page? |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=www.thaiairways.com}} === Airbus A321neo === In February 2024, Thai Airways entered into a lease agreement with AerCap for ten Airbus A321neo aircraft.{{Cite web |date=21 February 2024 |title=THAI AIRWAYS ORDERS 45 787S |url=https://www.airlineratings.com/news/passenger-news/thai-airways-orders-45-787s-and-options-777x/}} In addition, the airline finalized a separate agreement with SMBC Aviation Capital for the lease of eight additional A321neos.{{Cite web |title=SMBC Aviation Capital :: SMBC Aviation Capital signs lease agreements with Thai Airways for 8 Airbus A321neo aircraft |url=https://www.smbc.aero/news/2025/smbc-aviation-capital-signs-lease-agreements-thai-airways-8-airbus-a321neo-aircraft |access-date=6 February 2025 |website=www.smbc.aero}} On 22 April 2025, Thai Airways signed a lease agreement with China Aircraft Leasing Group for nine aircraft, marking the first collaboration between the two companies.{{Cite web |title=CALC |url=https://www.calc.com.hk/?route=press_detail&id=390 |access-date=23 April 2025 |website=www.calc.com.hk}} The following day, the airline further expanded its fleet through a lease agreement with BOC Aviation for five Airbus A321neos.{{Cite web |title=BOC AVIATION SIGNS LEASE AGREEMENT WITH THAI AIRWAYS FOR FIVE AIRBUS A321NEO AIRCRAFT |url=https://www.bocaviation.com/en/Press-Releases/2025/4/20250423---Thai-Airways-5-Airbus-A321NEO-aircraft |access-date=23 April 2025 |website=www.bocaviation.com}} In total, the airline has secured 32 aircraft under these lease agreements, significantly strengthening its narrow-body fleet. All aircraft will be equipped with the latest generation of Thompson Vantage seats, featuring 16 fully lie-flat beds in Business Class arranged in a 2-2 / 1-1 configuration. Each aircraft will also offer Wi-Fi connectivity and a new in-flight entertainment system to enhance the passenger experience.{{Cite web |title=Thai Airways CEO Chai Eamsiri on the Airline's Future |url=https://www.airwaysmag.com/new-post/discussing-thai-airways-ceo-chai-eamsiri?fbclid=IwY2xjawJcthZleHRuA2FlbQIxMAABHX2kjz6yeXC1ERTTdmG4gnWY_1Aiiyb0MXdLg2V3mTLbBS2GmDUSC-P0eQ_aem_0S7ywx8xVgo5yKdEwQeaVg |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=airwaysmag.com}}{{Cite web |title=Thompson Aero Seating announces A321neo programme for THAI |work=Thompson Aero |date=8 April 2025 |url=https://www.thompsonaero.com/news/thompson-aero-seating-announces-a321neo-programme-for-thai/ |author1=Tasadmin }} Thai Airways took delivery of its first A321neo on 24 December 2025, with its inaugural flight scheduled for 22 January 2026, on the Bangkok–Singapore route.{{Cite web |last=thanawan_win |date=25 December 2025 |title='การบินไทย' รับมอบเครื่องบิน Airbus A321neo ลำแรก จากทั้งหมด 32 ลำ เสริมแกร่งฝูงบิน |url=https://www.thansettakij.com/business/tourism/647492 |access-date=28 December 2025 |website=thansettakij |language=th}} === Airbus A330-300 === Thai Airways placed an order for twelve Airbus A330-300 aircraft, which were delivered to the airline between 1994 and 1998. The airline later placed additional orders and leases for another fifteen aircraft, delivered between 2009 and 2013. In 2018, three aircraft underwent a cabin retrofit program that equipped them with fully lie-flat Thomson Vantage seats in a “throne” seat configuration, while the older twelve aircraft were phased out between 2013 and 2017. Thai Airways later retired twelve of the fifteen remaining Airbus A330-300s, citing financial difficulties caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite news |title=Thai Airways to sell 42 jets, cut workforce to reduce costs |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/thai-airways-sell-42-jets-cut-workforce-reduce-costs-2021-11-01/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718002816/https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/thai-airways-sell-42-jets-cut-workforce-reduce-costs-2021-11-01/ |archive-date=18 July 2023 |access-date=17 October 2025 |work=Reuters |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Bordoloi |first=Pritam |date=11 February 2021 |title=Embattled carrier Thai Airways to retire all A380, A330 and 747 |url=https://internationalfinance.com/aviation/embattled-carrier-thai-airways-retire/ |access-date=17 October 2025 |website=International Finance |language=en-GB}} Following the airline’s financial recovery and the lifting of lockdown restrictions, Thai Airways signed a lease agreement with CDB Aviation for two used Airbus A330-300 aircraft on 2 January 2024. Both aircraft were formerly operated by [[Virgin Atlantic]] and were delivered in October 2024. They are equipped with 1-1-1 herringbone business class seats and a premium economy cabin. The airline later signed a lease agreement with [[Avolon]] for another used Airbus A330-300, also previously operated by Virgin Atlantic, which was delivered in August 2025. === Airbus A350-900 === Thai Airways announced a purchase deal for four Airbus A350-900s in 2011, along with lease agreements with Aviation Lease and Finance Company (ALAFCO) for six additional aircraft and two from CIT Aerospace International. All twelve aircraft were delivered between 2016 and 2018. The airline later signed lease agreements with various companies for eleven used Airbus A350-900s, the majority of which were previously operated by [[Hainan Airlines]] and delivered between 2023 and 2024.{{Cite web |date=21 February 2024 |title=AerCap Announces Lease Agreements with Thai Airways for Four Airbus A350-900 Aircraft, Three Boeing 787-9 Aircraft and Ten Airbus A321NEO Aircraft |url=https://www.aercap.com/news-media/press-releases/detail/555/aercap-announces-lease-agreements-with-thai-airways-for |access-date=17 October 2025 |website=AerCap Holdings N.V. |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Thai Airways adds A350-900 {{!}} News {{!}} Airfinance Global |url=https://platform.airfinanceglobal.com/articles/3593511/thai-airways-adds-a350-900 |access-date=17 October 2025 |website=platform.airfinanceglobal.com}} In 2025, [[Airbus]] and Thai Airways signed a [[Letter of intent|Letter of Intent]] to retrofit the Airbus A350-900 fleet. The retrofit will include new Business and Economy Class seats, the introduction of a Premium Economy Class, and improvements to in-flight entertainment. Retrofitting is expected to begin in 2028. === Boeing 777 === Thai Airways operates two Boeing 777 variants: three Boeing 777-200ERs and seventeen Boeing 777-300ERs. ==== Boeing 777-200ER ==== Six aircraft were purchased and delivered to Thai Airways in 2006. They are currently being phased out, with completion expected by 2029. ==== Boeing 777-300ER ==== Thai Airways initially leased five Boeing 777-300ERs from [[Jet Airways]] between 2011 and 2013, before the board of directors announced purchase and lease agreements for fourteen Boeing 777-300ERs on 13 June 2011. The batch was delivered between 2012 and 2015. The airline later signed a lease agreement with [[BOC Aviation]] for another three aircraft, which are equipped with Royal First Class cabins and were delivered in 2022.{{Cite news |last=Praprutitum |first=Kamolwat |date=8 April 2022 |title=Leased 777-300ERs to join THAI's fleet |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/general/2291894/leased-777-300ers-to-join-thais-fleet |access-date=17 October 2025 |work=Bangkok Post |language=en}} In 2025, the airline announced a cabin retrofit program for its fourteen Boeing 777-300ERs, which will soon be equipped with new business class seats featuring privacy doors and enhanced comfort. The new cabin configuration will also introduce a premium economy class and a 3-4-3 economy class layout. The airline also purchased four of the previously leased aircraft from BOC Aviation.{{Cite web |last=ฐานเศรษฐกิจ |date=26 March 2025 |title=การบินไทย ปิดดีลซื้อเครื่องบินโบอิ้ง 777-300 ER 4 ลำ เสริมฝูงบิน |url=https://www.thansettakij.com/business/tourism/623107 |access-date=17 October 2025 |website=thansettakij |language=th}} === Boeing 787 === Thai Airways currently operates two Boeing 787 variants: six Boeing 787-8s and three Boeing 787-9s, and will soon operate six Boeing 787-10s. ==== Boeing 787-8 ==== Thai Airways leased six Boeing 787-8s from International Lease Finance Corporation in 2011, which were delivered to the airline in 2014 and 2015. On 23 October 2025, the airline held its annual general meeting, where one of the main topics of discussion was the decision to lease 8–10 wide-body aircraft. The plans under consideration included two options: leasing eight Airbus A330-200s, previously operated by [[American Airlines]], from Jetran; or leasing ten Boeing 787-8s, previously operated by [[China Southern Airlines]], from Avolon. However, both options were initially rejected due to concerns over outdated technology.{{Cite web |last=ฐานเศรษฐกิจ |date=17 October 2025 |title=การบินไทย ลุยไฟ ดันเช่าเครื่องบินหมื่นล้าน ชิงตัดหน้า AGM ตั้งบอร์ดใหม่ |url=https://www.thansettakij.com/economy/641615 |access-date=17 October 2025 |website=thansettakij |language=th}}{{Cite web |date=25 October 2025 |title=เปิดผลกระทบ 'การบินไทย' หลังพลาดเช่า 'เครื่องบินใหม่' ปีนี้ |url=https://www.bangkokbiznews.com/business/economic/1204553 |access-date=7 November 2025 |website=bangkokbiznews |language=th}} Subsequently, the decision was revised, with Thai Airways choosing the latter option and proceeding to lease ten Boeing 787-8s from Avolon. The agreement is currently ongoing and is expected to be completed by February 2026, with a discount already offered by the lessor.{{Cite web |last=thanawan_win |date=19 January 2026 |title=‘การบินไทย’ เช่าเครื่องบินโบอิ้ง 787 รวม 10 ลำ เสริมฝูงบิน 100 ลำปีนี้ |url=https://www.thansettakij.com/business/tourism/649361 |access-date=20 January 2026 |website=thansettakij |language=th}} ==== Boeing 787-9 ==== Thai Airways announced plans to lease two Boeing 787-9s from ILFC in 2011, which were delivered to the airline in 2016. On 20 February 2024, Thai Airways announced an order for 45 Boeing 787-9s directly from Boeing, along with options for an additional 35 aircraft. These options can be converted to the larger Boeing 787-10 or the [[Boeing 777X]] series as the airline seeks to modernize and expand its widebody fleet and international network. Thai Airways’ Boeing 787-9s will be equipped with GEnx engines. To meet demand in high-traffic Asian markets, the airline converted six of its aircraft orders to the [[Boeing 787 Dreamliner|Boeing 787-10]]. These [[Boeing 787 Dreamliner|Boeing 787s]] will also feature new business class seats, premium economy, and economy class—similar to the retrofitted [[Boeing 777|Boeing 777-300ERs]]. Additionally, Thai Airways has signed lease agreements with [[AerCap]] for four [[Boeing 787 Dreamliner|Boeing 787-9s]]—one of which has already been delivered—and with Air Lease Corporation for another three.{{Cite web |author= |title=Air Lease Corporation Announces Lease Placement of Three New Boeing 787 Aircraft with Thai Airways International |url=https://airleasecorp.com/press/air-lease-corporation-announces-lease-placement-of-three-new-boeing-787-aircraft-with-thai-airways-international |access-date=7 November 2024 |website=Air Lease Corporation |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=21 February 2024 |title=AerCap Announces Lease Agreements with Thai Airways for Four Airbus A350-900 Aircraft, Three Boeing 787-9 Aircraft and Ten Airbus A321NEO Aircraft |url=https://www.aercap.com/news-media/press-releases/detail/555/aercap-announces-lease-agreements-with-thai-airways-for |access-date=7 November 2024 |website=AerCap Holdings N.V. |language=en |quote=The 787 deliveries are scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2024 through the fourth quarter of 2025}} In total, Thai Airways is scheduled to take delivery of 44 Boeing 787-9s and 6 Boeing 787-10s. Two of the Boeing 787-9s leased from AerCap were delivered in May 2024 and October 2025. ==Fleet History== === Airbus A340 === [[File:HS-TYV@PEK (20250205165724).jpg|thumb|One of the former Thai Airways [[Airbus A340|Airbus A340-500]] aircraft is currently in service with the [[Royal Thai Air Force]].]] Thai Airways initially ordered three Airbus A340-500s and four Airbus A340-600s in 2003, before adding one additional A340-500 and one A340-600 in 2004. The purpose of the order was for Thai Airways to operate direct non-stop flights from Bangkok to New York using the Airbus A340-500, which was configured with 60 business-class seats, 42 premium economy seats, and 113 economy-class seats, competing with Singapore Airlines. Meanwhile, the Airbus A340-600, configured with 8 first-class, 60 business-class, and 199 economy-class seats, was intended to operate non-stop flights from Bangkok to Los Angeles. The New York flight began on 1 May 2005 but was discontinued on 1 July 2008 due to major financial losses. The Los Angeles service was later converted to a one-stop flight via Incheon Airport in 2012, before being discontinued in 2015. After both routes were terminated, the aircraft were grounded at Don Mueang Airport and U-Tapao Airport and listed for sale on Thai Aircraft Trading website. One Airbus A340-500 was sold to the Royal Thai Air Force in 2016. The remaining aircraft were sold to Hua An Aviation Parts Co., Ltd. in 2022 and delivered to the company between 2024 and 2025.{{Cite web |title='Airbus A340' ฝูงบินเจ้าปัญหายุคทักษิณ ทำ 'บินไทย' ขาดทุนมหาศาล? |url=https://www.matichon.co.th/weekly/featured/article_32853#:~:text='Airbus%20A340'%20%E0%B8%9D%E0%B8%B9%E0%B8%87%E0%B8%9A%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%99%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%88%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%8D%E0%B8%AB%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%B8%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%97%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%A9%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%93%20%E0%B8%97%E0%B8%B3%20'%E0%B8%9A%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%99%E0%B9%84%E0%B8%97%E0%B8%A2'%20%E0%B8%82%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%97%E0%B8%B8%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%AB%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A8%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A5?%20%2D%20%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%95%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%8A%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B8%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%AB%E0%B9%8C%20Featured.}}{{Cite web |title=THAI Aircraft Trading |url=https://www.thaiaircrafttrading.com/aircraft.html?FLEET=A340 |access-date=20 October 2025 |website=www.thaiaircrafttrading.com}}{{Cite web |last=ฐานเศรษฐกิจดิจิทัล |date=25 August 2022 |title="การบินไทย"ขายเครื่องบินอีก14 ลำ มหากาพย์ A340 ขายออกแล้ว |url=https://www.thansettakij.com/business/tourism/537866 |access-date=20 October 2025 |website=thansettakij |language=th}} === Airbus A380 === [[File:Airbus A380-841, Thai Airways International AN2334366.jpg|thumb|[[Airbus A380|Airbus A380-800]]]] The airline ordered six Airbus A380-800s, which were delivered between 2012 and 2013. The aircraft were configured with 12 first-class seats, 60 business-class seats, and 435 economy-class seats, and operated on Thai Airways routes to Frankfurt, London Heathrow, Osaka Kansai, Paris Charles de Gaulle, and Tokyo Narita. The fleet was grounded in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and was initially expected to return to service in 2024. However, the plan to revive the aircraft was abandoned in 2022 due to high operating costs. All aircraft were stored at Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport and U-Tapao Airport and listed for sale on the Thai Aircraft Trading website.
